rule.name: Authentication Modules
rule.rule_desc: The checked code implements an identity, access-control, or abuse-prevention decision. Determine the trusted verifier, protected resources, and whether the control is enforced on every relevant path.
rule.vuln_desc: If identity or resource authorization can be bypassed, an attacker may impersonate a user, access another user’s data, or perform restricted operations. A control’s presence alone does not establish a weakness.
rule.developer: Enforce authentication and object-level authorization on the trusted server or privileged boundary. Use strong verifier material, appropriate rate limits and recovery controls, and test access by unauthenticated and insufficiently privileged callers.
rule.reviewer: Verify that authentication mechanisms are implemented securely, with protections like parameterized inputs, encryption, and secure session management. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: File Upload Functionality
rule.rule_desc: The application accepts uploaded content. Identify storage destinations, execution behavior, filename handling, and the effective size and type checks.
rule.vuln_desc: A crafted upload may execute as application code, overwrite files, disclose data through later processing, or exhaust storage if the upload crosses the intended content and filesystem boundaries.
rule.developer: Allowlist required file types, inspect content rather than trusting extensions, bound sizes, generate server-side names, and store uploads outside executable paths with appropriate access controls.
rule.reviewer: Verify that secure file upload practices are followed, including file type validation, size restrictions, and appropriate access controls to prevent unauthorized file uploads. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Server-side Secrets Handling
rule.rule_desc: The checked source or build configuration embeds potentially sensitive credential or key material. Determine whether it is active and whether it reaches distributed artifacts or logs.
rule.vuln_desc: A party who can read exposed source, artifacts, configuration, or logs may recover active secrets and access the protected service or decrypt data with the secret owner’s privileges.
rule.developer: Remove active secrets from source and build layers, rotate exposed values, and load replacements through a restricted secret-management facility. Use narrowly privileged, short-lived credentials.
rule.reviewer: Assess the handling of server-side secrets and verify if proper security measures are in place. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Credit Card
rule.rule_desc: The code handles private data or configures build and process hardening. Determine which information is retained and what protection the deployed artifact actually supplies.
rule.vuln_desc: Insufficient memory, diagnostic, or build protections may make private values easier to recover or increase the consequences of another defect. Their absence alone does not establish an exploit path.
rule.developer: Minimize private data lifetimes and diagnostic exposure, apply the platform’s appropriate hardening controls, and verify the final binary rather than inferring protection from source markers alone.
rule.reviewer: Assess the handling of credit card information and verify if proper security measures are in place. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Insecure HTTP Communication
rule.rule_desc: The checked source contains a transport-security exception, insecure endpoint, or certificate-validation configuration. Resolve the effective policy and the connections it governs.
rule.vuln_desc: An attacker on the network may read or alter affected traffic if sensitive data travels over cleartext or the connection accepts an untrusted server. Normal HTTPS endpoints and correctly implemented validation do not establish exposure.
rule.developer: Use HTTPS with normal certificate-chain and hostname verification. Remove permissive production callbacks and broad transport exceptions; restrict any justified exception to a documented, non-sensitive endpoint.
rule.reviewer: Review all URLs or network requests across source code, configuration files, and external API references to ensure HTTPS is used instead of HTTP. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Sensitive Debug Information
rule.rule_desc: The code writes diagnostic data or exposes detailed errors. Establish the values emitted, production configuration, and recipients of the output.
rule.vuln_desc: Readers of exposed diagnostics may obtain credentials, private records, internal paths, or implementation details that enable account misuse or targeted attacks.
rule.developer: Keep sensitive values and detailed errors out of user-facing responses and routine logs. Redact before emission, restrict diagnostic access, and verify production logging configuration.
rule.reviewer: Check for debug-related configurations in application settings and ensure that they are disabled or set to false in production environments to protect sensitive information. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Insecure SQL Query: Unsafe String Concatenation
rule.rule_desc: The checked source contains a database query or query-construction operation. Determine whether untrusted values can change statement structure and whether record access is authorized.
rule.vuln_desc: If externally controlled values enter query syntax, an attacker may read, change, or delete records or bypass data-access restrictions with the database connection’s privileges. Fixed queries and correctly bound parameters do not establish this condition.
rule.developer: Bind data values as parameters, choose dynamic identifiers from a fixed allowlist, and enforce object-level access checks. Trace the complete query construction before replacing a safe query.
rule.reviewer: Verify that SQL queries use parameterized queries or prepared statements to handle user input securely. flag any occurrences of unsafe string concatenation in SQL queries for further review. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: IPv4 / IPv6 Address
rule.rule_desc: The code declares an entry point, model, destination, or configuration value that may cross a trust boundary. Identify callers, recipients, and the required data-access policy.
rule.vuln_desc: A boundary that trusts unauthorized callers or exposes private output may permit data disclosure or state changes. A declaration, address, or architectural marker alone does not establish such a failure.
rule.developer: Trace the actual boundary, restrict accepted inputs and recipients, and enforce authentication and object-level authorization where required. Verify both authorized and denied use cases.
rule.reviewer: Check for appropriate input handling and assess the implementation of input validation and sanitization techniques for IP addresses. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: TODO Comments
rule.rule_desc: The code contains a maintainability, accessibility, or build-configuration review marker. Establish a concrete affected behavior before assigning security severity.
rule.vuln_desc: No direct confidentiality or integrity consequence is established by this marker alone. A related implementation defect could affect availability or prevent users from using essential controls, depending on the actual behavior.
rule.developer: Resolve the specific unfinished behavior, accessibility requirement, or build hygiene concern. Confirm its real operational effect and test the corrected behavior before classifying it as a security defect.
rule.reviewer: Check for the presence of TODO comments and verify if they have been properly addressed during code reviews and inspections. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Monkey Patched Code
rule.rule_desc: The code obtains executable material or replaces application behavior at runtime. Determine the origin, integrity checks, and intended deployment scope.
rule.vuln_desc: A party able to substitute executable material or a runtime hook may run code with application privileges, inspect protected data, or alter security checks.
rule.developer: Load only approved code from trusted locations, verify signatures or integrity before execution, and restrict runtime replacement to documented, authorized behavior.
rule.reviewer: Verify the presence of monkey patched code in the project and assess its impact on code stability and security. Particular attention should be paid to patches affecting security-critical components like authentication, authorization, or database queries. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Insecure Cryptographic Algorithm
rule.rule_desc: The checked source uses a random generator, cryptographic primitive, or initialization value whose suitability depends on its security purpose and inputs.
rule.vuln_desc: Predictable secrets or unsuitable cryptographic parameters may enable credential guessing, reveal plaintext, or weaken integrity when used to protect security-sensitive data. Non-security hashes and identifiers do not establish this condition.
rule.developer: Use a cryptographically secure generator for secrets and modern purpose-appropriate cryptography. Use unique nonces, protected keys, and a vetted password-hashing scheme where passwords are stored.
rule.reviewer: Verify that secure cryptographic algorithms are used to mitigate the risk of cryptographic vulnerabilities. Assess whether deprecated or weak algorithms are used and recommend replacing them with stronger alternatives. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.
